proclaim.title: Linking Sentences Together
proclaim.subtitle: 第零课 · 连接句子
proclaim.explanation: Before tackling discourse markers, testimony, and the gospel sequence, there's a smaller skill worth building first: saying two or three plain sentences in a row, connected, without a listener prompting you between each one. This is the actual bridge between short dialogue exchanges and everything else in this track.

points.label: Start smaller than you think
points.detail: Two connected sentences is a real, complete skill — not a lesser version of a longer speech. Master this before adding more.

points.label: 然后 (then) is the simplest connector
points.detail: It links one action or idea to the next without needing anything fancy — 我先读经，然后祷告 (I read Scripture first, then pray).

points.label: 因为...所以... (because...so...) links a reason to a result
points.detail: One of the most common patterns in real speech, including everything from Discourse Markers ahead.

points.label: Say it out loud, not just in your head
points.detail: Reading a sentence silently and actually saying two linked sentences aloud are different skills — this track is about speaking, so practice speaking.

examples.chinese: 我先读经，然后祷告。
examples.pinyin: wǒ xiān dú jīng， rán hòu dǎo gào。
examples.english: I read Scripture first, then I pray.
examples.note: Two actions linked with 然后.

examples.chinese: 因为神爱我们，所以耶稣来了。
examples.pinyin: yīn wèi shén ài wǒ men， suǒ yǐ yē sū lái le。
examples.english: Because God loves us, Jesus came.
examples.note: A reason linked to a result with 因为...所以...

examples.chinese: 我以前不认识神，后来朋友带我去教会。
examples.pinyin: wǒ yǐ qián bù rèn shí shén， hòu lái péng yǒu dài wǒ qù jiào huì。
examples.english: I didn't know God before; later, a friend brought me to church.
examples.note: Two connected ideas — the same shape a testimony's opening needs.

examples.chinese: 我们先唱诗，然后听讲道，最后一起祷告。
examples.pinyin: wǒ men xiān chàng shī， rán hòu tīng jiǎng dào， zuì hòu yì qǐ dǎo gào。
examples.english: We sing first, then hear the sermon, and finally pray together.
examples.note: Three linked actions — one step further than two.

practice.question: What's the simplest word to link one action to the next?
Which pattern links a reason to a result?
"我先读经，然后祷告" means...
options: I read Scripture first, then I pray
I want to read Scripture or pray
I never read Scripture or pray
practice.answer: I read Scripture first, then I pray

practice.question: What's the actual goal of this lesson?
options: Saying two or three linked sentences aloud, not just silently
Memorizing as many connectors as possible
Skipping ahead to the hardest lesson first
practice.answer: Saying two or three linked sentences aloud, not just silently

proclaim.title: Discourse Markers for Speaking
proclaim.subtitle: 第一课 · 演讲连接词
proclaim.explanation: Holding a conversation and giving a short talk are different skills. A testimony, a devotional, or a gospel presentation needs connecting words that string several sentences together into one flow — words this app's conversational lessons never needed, since dialogue is short back-and-forth, not one person speaking at length.

points.label: 首先 / 其次 / 最后
points.detail: Firstly / secondly / finally — the basic skeleton for any structured talk with multiple points.

points.label: 换句话说
points.detail: "In other words" — useful for restating an idea more simply, which matters a lot when explaining faith to someone new to it.

points.label: 总结来说
points.detail: "In summary" — signals you're wrapping up, so listeners know a conclusion is coming.

points.label: 让我们一起
points.detail: "Let's together..." — a common way to invite a group into an action: praying, reading, reflecting.

points.label: 不但...而且...
points.detail: "Not only... but also..." — for building an idea in two connected parts, common in testimony and preaching.

examples.chinese: 首先，我想分享神在我生命中做的一件事。
examples.pinyin: shǒu xiān， wǒ xiǎng fēn xiǎng shén zài wǒ shēng mìng zhòng zuò de yī jiàn shì。
examples.english: Firstly, I'd like to share something God has done in my life.

examples.chinese: 换句话说，恩典是我们不配得到，却白白得到的。
examples.pinyin: huàn jù huà shuō， ēn diǎn shì wǒ men bù pèi dé dào， què bái bái dé dào de。
examples.english: In other words, grace is something we don't deserve, yet receive freely.

examples.chinese: 不但如此，神也赦免了我一切的罪。
examples.pinyin: bù dàn rú cǐ， shén yě shè miǎn le wǒ yī qiè de zuì。
examples.english: Not only that, God also forgave all my sins.

examples.chinese: 总结来说，这就是我信主的原因。
examples.pinyin: zǒng jié lái shuō， zhè jiù shì wǒ xìn zhǔ de yuán yīn。
examples.english: In summary, this is why I believe in the Lord.

practice.question: Which word means "firstly"?
What does 换句话说 signal?
Which phrase means "in summary"?
"不但...而且..." is used to...
options: Build an idea in two connected parts
practice.answer: Build an idea in two connected parts

practice.question: Which phrase invites a group into a shared action?

proclaim.title: Telling Your Story
proclaim.subtitle: 第二课 · 分享你的见证
proclaim.explanation: Every testimony has the same basic three-act shape: what life was like before, what changed, and what's different now. Learning this structure — and the words that mark each part — makes it possible to tell your own story, not just recognize someone else's.

points.label: 以前 — before
points.detail: Sets the scene: what your life or thinking was like before this turning point.

points.label: 后来 / 就在那时候 — then / that's when
points.detail: Marks the turning point itself — the moment something changed.

points.label: 从此 / 现在 — since then / now
points.detail: Describes what's different in your life now, as a result.

points.label: A simple three-sentence scaffold
points.detail: 以前，我___。后来，___。从此，我___。 ("Before, I ___. Then, ___. Since then, I ___.") You can build a real testimony on just this shape.

examples.chinese: 以前，我不认识神。
examples.pinyin: yǐ qián， wǒ bù rèn shí shén。

examples.chinese: 后来，一位朋友带我去教会。
examples.pinyin: hòu lái， yī wèi péng yǒu dài wǒ qù jiào huì。
examples.english: Then, a friend brought me to church.

examples.chinese: 就在那时候，我明白了神的爱。
examples.pinyin: jiù zài nà shí hòu， wǒ míng bái le shén de ài。
examples.english: That's when I understood God's love.

examples.chinese: 从此，我的生命完全不一样了。
examples.pinyin: cóng cǐ， wǒ de shēng mìng wán quán bù yí yàng le。
examples.english: Since then, my life has been completely different.

practice.question: Which word sets up "what life was like before"?
Which phrase marks the turning point itself?
Which word describes life after the change?
What are the three parts of this testimony structure, in order?

yourTurn.prompt: Try writing 2-3 sentences of your own testimony using this structure. This isn't graded — it's just yours to keep and revisit.

proclaim.title: The Gospel in Order
proclaim.subtitle: 第三课 · 有次序地传福音
proclaim.explanation: Lesson 33 (back in the main lessons) modeled one realistic gospel conversation. This is different: a short, memorizable *sequence* of verses — sometimes called the "Romans Road" — that you can deliver on your own, start to finish, without needing someone else's side of a dialogue to prompt you.

points.label: 1. Everyone has sinned
points.detail: Romans 3:23 — the problem: sin separates everyone from God's glory.

points.label: 2. The consequence and the gift
points.detail: Romans 6:23 — sin's wage is death; God's gift is eternal life in Christ.

points.label: 3. God's love and the solution
points.detail: John 3:16 — God's response to the problem: sending His Son.

points.label: 4. How to respond
points.detail: Romans 10:9 — confess with your mouth, believe in your heart.

points.label: Practicing the sequence
points.detail: Read all four aloud, in order, without stopping. That's the actual skill — not just recognizing each verse alone.

examples.chinese: 因为世人都犯了罪，亏缺了神的荣耀；
examples.pinyin: yīn wèi shì rén dōu fàn le zuì， kuī quē le shén de róng yào；

examples.chinese: 因为罪的工价乃是死；惟有神的恩赐，在我们的主基督耶稣里，乃是永生。
examples.pinyin: yīn wèi zuì de gōng jià nǎi shì sǐ； wéi yǒu shén de ēn cì， zài wǒ men de zhǔ jī dū yē sū lǐ， nǎi shì yǒng shēng。

examples.chinese: 神爱世人，甚至将他的独生子赐给他们，叫一切信他的，不至灭亡，反得永生。
examples.pinyin: shén ài shì rén， shèn zhì jiāng tā de dú shēng zi cì gěi tā men， jiào yī qiè xìn tā de， bù zhì miè wáng， fǎn dé yǒng shēng。

examples.chinese: 你若口里认耶稣为主，心里信神叫他从死里复活，就必得救。
examples.pinyin: nǐ ruò kǒu lǐ rèn yē sū wéi zhǔ， xīn lǐ xìn shén jiào tā cóng sǐ lǐ fù huó， jiù bì děi jiù。

practice.question: What is the first step in this sequence?
According to Romans 6:23, what is God's gift?
Which verse describes God's response to the problem of sin?
According to Romans 10:9, what are the two things someone does to respond?
options: Confess with the mouth, believe in the heart
practice.answer: Confess with the mouth, believe in the heart

practice.question: What is the value of practicing all four verses in order?
options: Being able to deliver the whole sequence unprompted
practice.answer: Being able to deliver the whole sequence unprompted

proclaim.title: Answering Common Questions
proclaim.subtitle: 第四课 · 回答常见的疑问
proclaim.explanation: Sharing the gospel with Chinese speakers often runs into specific objections tied to family and culture — different from generic Western skepticism. Recognizing these, and having a calm, respectful response ready, matters more than having a perfect argument.

points.label: "We're Chinese, we have our own beliefs"
points.detail: 我们是中国人，有自己的信仰 — often about identity and heritage, not really a claim about truth. Respond by honoring their heritage while gently distinguishing culture from faith.

points.label: "What will my family think?"
points.detail: 家人会怎么想？ — reflects real fear of family conflict or dishonoring ancestors. This deserves genuine empathy, not a rushed answer.

points.label: "Isn't this just a Western religion?"
points.detail: 这不是西方的宗教吗？ — like the family objection, this deserves acknowledgment before information: many people wonder this. Then, worth knowing: Christianity's roots are in the Middle East, and it has been present in China for centuries — not a fact to win an argument with, but something to offer gently.

points.label: "There are so many religions — how do you know?"
points.detail: 宗教这么多，你怎么知道哪个对？ — an honest question worth taking seriously, not deflecting.

points.label: "What do I do when my family does ancestor rituals?"
points.detail: 家里拜拜的时候，我要怎么办？ — this isn't a one-time fear, it's a recurring practical tension for many new believers with non-Christian families. There's rarely one universally correct answer; being present respectfully without participating in the ritual itself is a common approach, but this is genuinely worth discussing with a pastor or mentor who knows the specific family situation, not resolving alone.

examples.chinese: 信耶稣不是要你不孝敬父母。
examples.pinyin: xìn yē sū bú shì yào nǐ bù xiào jìng fù mǔ。
examples.english: Believing in Jesus doesn't mean you stop honoring your parents.
examples.note: A gentle, respectful response to the family-honor objection.

examples.chinese: 这个问题很多人都问过。基督教其实很早就传到中国了。
examples.pinyin: zhè ge wèn tí hěn duō rén dōu wèn guò。 jī dū jiào qí shí hěn zǎo jiù chuán dào zhōng guó le。
examples.english: Many people ask this. Christianity actually reached China quite early in history.
examples.note: Acknowledges the question is common before offering the historical point — not a debate-winning fact dropped cold.

examples.chinese: 我明白你的担心，我们可以慢慢聊。
examples.pinyin: wǒ míng bái nǐ de dān xīn， wǒ men kě yǐ màn màn liáo。
examples.english: I understand your concern, we can talk about this slowly.
examples.note: A patient opening line when someone raises a real fear.

examples.chinese: 每个宗教都有道理，但我自己经历过耶稣的爱，想邀请你也来看看。
examples.pinyin: měi gè zōng jiào dōu yǒu dào lǐ， dàn wǒ zì jǐ jīng lì guò yē sū de ài， xiǎng yāo qǐng nǐ yě lái kàn kàn。
examples.english: Every religion has its reasoning, but I've personally experienced Jesus's love, and I want to invite you to see for yourself too.
examples.note: A personal, experiential response to "how do you know" — not an attempt to out-argue every other religion.

examples.chinese: 这是一个很好的问题。
examples.pinyin: zhè shì yí gè hěn hǎo de wèn tí。
examples.note: A respectful way to receive a genuine objection, not dismiss it.

practice.question: When someone raises an objection, what should generally come first — information or empathy?
options: Empathy — acknowledging the question before offering information
practice.answer: Empathy — acknowledging the question before offering information

practice.question: What's a genuine, honest way to respond to "how do you know Christianity is true, with so many religions out there?"
options: A personal, experiential answer about your own faith
A comparative-religion debate to prove other religions wrong
practice.answer: A personal, experiential answer about your own faith

practice.question: Believing in Jesus means you should stop honoring your parents.
options: False — a common misunderstanding worth gently correcting
practice.answer: False — a common misunderstanding worth gently correcting

practice.question: What's the best approach when a new believer asks what to do during family ancestor rituals?
options: Discuss it with a pastor or mentor who knows their specific family situation
Give one universal rule that applies to everyone
Tell them to avoid the question entirely
practice.answer: Discuss it with a pastor or mentor who knows their specific family situation

proclaim.title: Following a Sermon
proclaim.subtitle: 第五课 · 听懂一篇讲道
proclaim.explanation: Scripture Reading Practice (in the main lessons) works with single verses. The full Bible (in Read) has no support at all. This is the bridge between them: a real, connected passage — Peter's sermon at Pentecost, the first Christian sermon ever preached — at a length closer to what you'd actually hear preached aloud.

points.label: 施行异能、奇事神迹
points.detail: "performed miracles, wonders, and signs" — a formal three-part phrase common in describing God's power in narrative Chinese.

points.label: 钉在十字架上
points.detail: "nailed to the cross" / crucified — already familiar from earlier lessons, reinforced here in a denser narrative context.

points.label: 扎心
points.detail: literally "pierced the heart" — describes being deeply, emotionally convicted, not just intellectually persuaded.

points.label: 悔改，奉耶稣基督的名受洗
points.detail: "repent, and be baptised in the name of Jesus Christ" — Peter's actual altar-call response, word for word.

examples.chinese: 「以色列人哪，请听我的话：神借着拿撒勒人耶稣在你们中间施行异能、奇事神迹，将他证明出来，这是你们自己知道的。
examples.pinyin: 「 yǐ sè liè rén nǎ， qǐng tīng wǒ de huà： shén jiè zhe ná sā lēi rén yē sū zài nǐ men zhōng jiān shī xíng yì néng、 qí shì shén jì， jiāng tā zhèng míng chū lái， zhè shì nǐ men zì jǐ zhī dào de。

examples.chinese: 他既按着神的定旨先见被交与人，你们就借着无法之人的手，把他钉在十字架上杀了。
examples.pinyin: tā jì àn zhe shén de dìng zhǐ xiān jiàn bèi jiāo yǔ rén， nǐ men jiù jiè zhe wú fǎ zhī rén de shǒu， bǎ tā dīng zài shí zì jià shàng shā le。

examples.chinese: 神却将死的痛苦解释了，叫他复活，因为他原不能被死拘禁。
examples.pinyin: shén què jiāng sǐ de tòng kǔ jiě shì le， jiào tā fù huó， yīn wèi tā yuán bù néng bèi sǐ jū jìn。

examples.chinese: 「故此，以色列全家当确实的知道，你们钉在十字架上的这位耶稣，神已经立他为主，为基督了。」
examples.pinyin: 「 gù cǐ， yǐ sè liè quán jiā dāng què shí de zhī dào， nǐ men dīng zài shí zì jià shàng de zhè wèi yē sū， shén yǐ jīng lì tā wéi zhǔ， wèi jī dū le 。」

examples.chinese: 众人听见这话，觉得扎心，就对彼得和其余的使徒说：「弟兄们，我们当怎样行？」
examples.pinyin: zhòng rén tīng jiàn zhè huà， jué de zhā xīn， jiù duì bǐ dé hé qí yú de shǐ tú shuō ：「 dì xiōng men， wǒ men dāng zěn yàng xíng ？」

examples.chinese: 彼得说：「你们各人要悔改，奉耶稣基督的名受洗，叫你们的罪得赦，就必领受所赐的圣灵；
examples.pinyin: bǐ dé shuō ：「 nǐ men gè rén yào huǐ gǎi， fèng yē sū jī dū de míng shòu xǐ， jiào nǐ men de zuì dé shè， jiù bì lǐng shòu suǒ cì de shèng líng；
